analyst_assessment: Curmudgeon's c14 H5 reading is correct and the gap is real. The vise's 'What the dome could do' h3 currently lists four carve-outs the dome periodically deploys — Chebychev-low-pass, bedrock difference, instrumental noise, parameter shift — and gives the bedrock and Chebychev rescues dedicated paragraph-level treatment (the former because it has a published-prior anchor in κ's 'Bedrock Induction Ratio' naming; the latter as the most methodologically plausible-sounding rescue, with its own three-fact dissection). The 'appeal to instrumental noise' currently appears only inline in the four-carve-out enumeration — no dedicated treatment, no D-122 anchor, no pointer to WIN-014. WIN-014's EXP-618 paragraph closes the sensitivity defense via an instrument-class tu-quoque (κ's denominator was measured with the same Wang et al. 2000 LaCoste-Romberg D-series spring D-122 whose ±3–4 µGal residual band the rescue invokes; coherent contact-time stacking across the eight-instrument 2009 network at √8 ≈ 2.8× suppression gives a network floor ~1.1–1.4 µGal, still 2–8× below the 3–9 µGal on-path prediction; sufficient insensitivity to have hidden the 2009 prediction is sufficient insensitivity to have manufactured the 1997 founding dip at 2.4–2.6σ on its own instrument's stated floor). The vise gap is therefore a cross-surface catalog problem, not an argument-construction problem — the argument exists at WIN-014, fully curmudgeon-vetted; the vise just needs to name the class member with a working pointer. Insertion point: immediately after the Chebychev-rescue dissection paragraph (which itself comes after the bedrock-rescue paragraph), before the OTS-canary close-out — matches the existing pattern of bedrock→Chebychev→OTS-close, extending it to bedrock→Chebychev→sensitivity→OTS-close. Word count ~280 (vs Chebychev's ~700 and bedrock's ~280) — appropriately scoped since the substance lives at WIN-014 and this is a summary-with-pointer.
kernel_of_truth: The sensitivity defense is structurally the strongest of the four post-hoc rescues — the LaCoste-Romberg precision figure (instrument-class ±3–4 µGal) is real and is the dome's own source's number. A defender is correct that a single spring gravimeter operating near its own residual floor cannot independently confirm a 3–9 µGal pulse against background tides. The new vise paragraph credits that observation up front and then uses it against the dome: the same instrument-class precision claim is also the ceiling on κ's denominator, and coherent contact-time stacking across eight 2009 instruments pushes the network floor an order of magnitude below the prediction band — so the sensitivity claim destroys κ's left-hand side faster than it shelters κ's right-hand side. The kernel is acknowledged; the closure uses it as its own undoing.

The instrument-sensitivity defense — that the LaCoste-Romberg spring gravimeters dominating the 2009 Chinese campaign (and, for the SG-053 question, the 1999 Membach SG) simply lacked the precision to register a κ-coupled pulse — is closed in WIN-014’s detail by an instrument-class tu-quoque. The same Wang et al. 2000 LaCoste-Romberg D-series spring (instrument D-122 at Mohe — Wang et al. 2000, Phys. Rev. D 62, 041101(R)) supplies κ’s 6.5 µGal denominator at its own authors’ stated 2–3 µGal precision and ±3–4 µGal single-instrument residual band; coherently stacked at each site’s known contact times across the eight-instrument 2009 network, that band suppresses by √8 ≈ 2.8× to ~1.1–1.4 µGal, still 2–8× below the 3–9 µGal on-path κ prediction. The rescue cannot save κ’s right-hand side without retracting κ’s left-hand side: sufficient instrument-class insensitivity to have hidden the 2009 prediction is also sufficient instrument-class insensitivity to have manufactured the 1997 founding signal, which Wang et al. 2000 reports at 6.0 ± 2.5 and 7.0 ± 2.7 µGal — a 2.4–2.6σ excursion on an instrument operating at its own stated floor. The same research group’s 2002 reanalysis (Yang & Wang 2002) under additional measurement controls found “no significant anomaly during the very solar eclipse,” and the 2013 record of the 2009 campaign — co-authored by Wang Qian-Shen and Hua Chang-Cai, both authors of the 1997 paper — attributes the original anomaly to “the drastic changes in the weather.” The discoverer team ran the better experiment and withdrew the original signal. See WIN-014 (Refuted by Data) for the full closure, including the off-totality coverage-scaling subcase and the SG-053 station-assignment moot.
